summary: Path parsing, normalisation and suffix-based transform inference. StoragePath is a classmethod-only helper (identify_scheme, normalize, join, to_str, matches) over universal_pathlib UPath and urllib, rejecting mixed-case schemes for strict SchemeSpecs and scheme: forms missing '//'. infer_pipeline parses a path's suffix chain right-to-left (.gz/.gzip -> Gzip, .gpg/.asc/.pgp -> GPG) into a Pipeline. The s3 submodule extracts bucket/key for any S3-family scheme. infer_pipeline and SUFFIX_TRANSFORMS work on a base install, while StoragePath and s3 need [http].
key_classes: StoragePath — stateless classmethod helper for scheme identification, strict normalisation, joining and wildcard matching; does not dispatch to backends
_GenericSchemePath — private str subclass returned by normalize() for SCHEMES entries UPath cannot construct; supports '/' joining
key_functions: StoragePath.identify_scheme(path) -> str | None — canonical scheme, '' for bare/local, None for unknown (aliases resolved, case-insensitive)
StoragePath.normalize(path) — canonical UPath/_GenericSchemePath; strips trailing slashes; ValueError on unknown scheme, mixed case, or missing '//'
StoragePath.join(path, name) — normalize(path) / stripped name; None if either is falsy
infer_pipeline(path, *, gpg=None, gzip=None) -> tuple[Pipeline | None, str] — suffix-chain inference; ValueError when a gpg suffix appears without gpg=
s3.s3_bucket(path, *, assume_s3=False) / s3.s3_key(path, *, assume_s3=False) — S3-family bucket/key extraction; None for non-addressable paths (including host:port netlocs)
extension_points: New schemes are added in _schemes.SCHEMES (not here); the S3-family scheme set in s3.py is derived from SCHEMES so it tracks new aliases automatically
Suffix inference is a fixed SUFFIX_TRANSFORMS table; supplying gzip=/gpg= instances customises the transforms used
lifecycle_notes: Package __init__ eagerly imports suffixes (base-install safe) and lazily imports StoragePath/s3 via __getattr__, raising MissingExtraError for [http]
Inference is read-side only; there is no write-side suffix inference
Parsing stops at the first unknown suffix, so 'a.gz.csv' yields no pipeline
documentation_hooks: Path normalisation rules: aliases, strict casing, trailing slashes, '//' requirement
Suffix inference reference: suffix table, ordering (outermost first), GPG key requirement
S3 bucket/key helpers and the assume_s3 bare-path mode
risks: normalize() returns UPath for fsspec-known schemes but a plain str subclass for others (e.g. azure, b2, smb); callers must treat the result via str() and cannot rely on Path methods
_normalize_bare calls expanduser(), so '~' in bare paths is expanded silently
StoragePath.identify_scheme and the module-level location.identify_scheme overlap; the canonical owner of scheme identification is location/_schemes
